newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court annuls sleaze probe of Paris mayor.
newsitem.headline: French court annuls sleaze probe of Paris mayor.

text.p: A court on Friday annulled on technical grounds a judicial investigation into allegations that the Gaullist mayor of Paris, Jean Tiberi, and his wife illegally received cash from public funds.

Acting on a motion by the mayor's lawyers, the court ruled that an investigating magistrate had used incorrect procedure in seizing a report for which Tiberi's wife Xaviere was paid by a local authority during a search of their Paris apartment.

A state prosecutor told the court last month that judge Eric Halphen had failed to record in his official account of the search how he had confiscated a copy of the report and later had the original sent from the Paris city hall.
He also said Halphen failed to use the correct legal procedure to report his questioning of Xaviere Tiberi.

Tiberi, re-elected to parliament last month, was placed under investigation this year over the payment of 200,000 francs ($35,000) to his wife by the Essonne district council in exchange for a 36-page report on prospects for economic links between Essonne and French-speaking nations.
The report was largely composed of truisms copied from a book and it was riddled with spelling mistakes.
The court also annulled the inquiry against Xaviere Tiberi, whose husband was alleged to have negotiated the payment with the fellow Gaullist Essonne council leader, Xavier Dugoin.
The investigation targeting Dugoin was dropped as well.
"This decision takes notice of the irregular nature of the search conducted by Eric Halphen," Dugoin's lawyer Alexandre Varaut said in a statement.

"Xavier Dugoin is pleased by the decision, which puts an end to legal action without foundation; the procedural fault cited by the court does not hide the reality that Xavier Dugoin is and remains innocent of the acts he was accused of in the Tiberi affair," it said.
Tiberi, who succeeded President and fellow Gaullist Jacques Chirac as the French capital's mayor in 1995, remains a focus of two other inquiries.

One concerns suspected illicit funding of his Gaullist RPR party by Paris municipal housing authority and the other involves a scandal over the letting of city-owned flats to political associates and relatives at lower than market rents.
Tiberi has denied any wrongdoing and has vowed to stay in office.
